paper.title: Regret Analysis for Continuous Dueling Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Cost-based continuous dueling bandit (noisy comparison feedback)
unmapped: P(a > a') = sigma(f(a') - f(a)) with cost f twice continuously differentiable and link sigma three times differentiable, rotation-symmetric, with positive non-increasing derivative on [0,B]
Learner needs link-function constants l_0, L_0, B_2, L_2 to tune lambda, mu, eta
Regret measured via minimum win probability P*(a) = inf_a' P(a > a')
settings.definition_quote: Reg_T^{DB}=\sup_{a\in{\cal A}}\bbE\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\{(P^{\ast}(a) - P^{\ast}(a_t)) + (P^{\ast}(a) - P^{\ast}(a'_t))\right\}\right]. ... Let an action space ${\cal A}\subset\R^d$ be compact convex set with non-empty interior.

settings.name_in_paper: Convex optimization with noisy comparison feedback
unmapped: P(a > a') = sigma(f(a') - f(a)) with link sigma satisfying Assumption 3
Learner needs link-function constants l_0, L_0, B_2, L_2
settings.definition_quote: In convex optimization with noisy comparison feedback, the learner chooses a pair $(a_t, a'_t)$ of actions in the learning process and suffers a loss $f(a_t)+f(a'_t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Convex optimization with noisy comparison feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Link function is the CDF of a zero-mean Gaussian with variance 2
settings.definition_quote: Assume that the action space $\calA$ is the $d$-dimensional unit Euclidean ball $\B_d$ and that the link function $\sigma_{\calG}$ is the cumulative distribution function of the zero-mean Gaussian random variable with variance $2$.

algorithms.name: NC-SMD (Noisy Comparison-based Stochastic Mirror Descent)
requires_knowledge_of: link constants l_0, L_0, B_2, L_2

symbols.C_thm: nu + (B_2 L^2 + (L+1) L_0 beta)/(2 lambda), with nu the self-concordance parameter
symbols.L_0: upper bound on link derivative sigma' on [-B,B]

conditions: Assumptions 1-3: cost f twice continuously differentiable, L-Lipschitz, alpha-strongly convex, beta-smooth; link sigma three times differentiable, rotation-symmetric, sigma' positive and non-increasing on [0,B]
nu-self-concordant barrier with full-rank Hessian and gradient onto R^d

source.label: thm2
source.quote: We set $C:=\nu + \frac{ B_2L^2 +(L+1)L_0\beta}{2\lambda}$. When the tuning parameters satisfy $\lambda\le l_0\alpha/2$, $\mu \ge \left(L_0^3 L_2/\lambda\right)^2$ and the total number $T$ of rounds satisfies $T\ge C\log T$. Algorithm \ref{A1} with a $\nu$-self-concordant function and the learning parameter $\eta=\frac{1}{2d}\sqrt{\frac{C\log T }{T}}$ achieves the following regret bound under Assumptions \ref{ass1}-\ref{ass3}: Reg_T^{DB}\le4d\sqrt{C T\log T}+2LL_0R.

results.notes: Regret defined via win probabilities in expectation (pseudo-regret type). R is the diameter of A (diam_K), L the Lipschitz constant of f (L_lip). Paper's C renamed C_thm to avoid clash with corruption budget.

tuning: output averaged action bar a_T = (1/2T) sum_t (a_t + a'_t)

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{ass1}-\ref{ass3}, the averaged action $\bar{a}_T$ satisfies the following when $T\ge C\log T$: \bbE[f(\bar{a}_T) - f(a^{\ast})]\le\frac{1}{l_0} \left(2d\sqrt{\frac{\nu\log T +C}{T}} + \frac{LL_0R}{T}\right)

results.notes: Optimization error of averaged action, recorded as simple_regret. Expression copied as stated (it does not exactly follow from Theorem thm2's algebra but recorded verbatim).

conditions: action space is the d-dimensional unit Euclidean ball
link is the CDF of N(0,2)
hard function is twice continuously differentiable, 0.5-strongly convex and 3.5-smooth

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Assume that the action space $\calA$ is the $d$-dimensional unit Euclidean ball $\B_d$ and that the link function $\sigma_{\calG}$ is the cumulative distribution function of the zero-mean Gaussian random variable with variance $2$. Let the number of rounds $T$ be fixed. Then, for any algorithm with noisy comparison feedback, there exists a function $f$ over $\B_d$ which is twice continuously differentiable, $0.5$-strongly convex and $3.5$-smooth such that the output $a_T$ of the algorithm satisfies \bbE[f(a_T) - f(a^*)]\ge 0.004 \min\left\{1, \frac{d}{\sqrt{2T}}\right\}.

results.notes: Obtained by reduction from Shamir (2013) Theorem 7 with noisy function feedback (two Gaussian evaluations per comparison).
